newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says NZ tax take concerns unwarranted.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ tax take concerns unwarranted.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters on Wednesday criticised recent commentary on a fall in government revenues from company taxation, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
Speaking to a parliamentary committee, Peters said that economists suggesting that the economy had gone down the tubes were wrong.

"Far from it. Company profit growth has been lower than expected. But in addition the Treasury December forecast underestimated the extent to which companies over-paid the provisional tax in the previous financial year," he said.
"The gloomy prognosis (by commentators) reflected either an incomplete representation of the facts or an incomplete understanding of what is driving recent changes in tax collection."
The figures were disclosed in the Government's current year fiscal update released on May 21.
Peters said that nearly half the decline in revenue from company tax had been offset by increases in other tax collections.
Changes in the international tax regime had also impacted on the company tax data.

The fiscal update when released had shown a NZ$566 million fall in company tax since the last forecast was released in December. This was partially offset by a $211 million rise in revenues from non-resident withholding tax.
